subject: general
question: IBM 370 was a _________ generation computer.
solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd**__ generation computer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• IBM 370 series, introduced in 1970, belongs to the 3rd generation of computers.
 
• 3rd generation computers used Integrated Circuits (ICs) to replace transistors, leading to more compact and efficient systems.
 
• These computers were characterized by the use of semiconductor memory and operating systems capable of multitasking and time-sharing.
 
• IBM 370 was known for being one of the first computers to support virtual memory, which allowed for more efficient processing and use of resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Generation Computers (1940-1956)**

 
 
• These computers used vacuum tubes for circuitry and magnetic drums for memory.
 
• They were very large, consumed a lot of power, and produced a lot of heat.
 
• Examples include ENIAC, UNIVAC.
 
 
 
• **Second Generation Computers (1956-1963)**
 
 
• These computers used transistors instead of vacuum tubes, making them smaller, faster, and more reliable.
 
• They also used magnetic core memory.
 
• Examples include IBM 1401 and IBM 7090.
 
 
 
• **Third Generation Computers (1964-1971)**
 
 
• Integrated Circuits (ICs) were used in these computers, which significantly increased the speed and efficiency.
 
• They also introduced operating systems and multiprogramming.
 
• Examples include IBM 360 and IBM 370.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Generation Computers (1971-Present)**
 
 
• These computers use microprocessors, which contain thousands of integrated circuits on a single silicon chip.
 
• They are characterized by the development of personal computers (PCs).
 
• Examples include Apple II, IBM PC.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Generation Computers (Present and Beyond)**
 
 
• These computers are based on artificial intelligence and use parallel processing and superconductors.
 
• They aim to develop devices that respond to natural language input and are capable of learning and self-organization.
 
• Examples include AI systems, advanced robotics.
